claim: DGGW's master heat-trace expansion (Theorem 4.8) writes the trace as I_0 plus a sum over all O-strata N of I_N/|Iso(N)|, where I_N := (4πt)^{-dim(N)/2} Σ_k t^k ∫_N b_k(N,x) dvol_N(x), giving an overall expansion of the form (4πt)^{-dim(O)/2} Σ_j c_j t^{j/2} (their eq. 4.9).
scope_conditions: any closed Riemannian orbifold O, any dimension
quoted_support: The heat trace Σ e^{-λ_j t} of O is asymptotic as t→0+ to I_0 + Σ_{N∈S(O)} I_N/|Iso(N)| ... This asymptotic expansion is of the form (4.9) (4πt)^{-dim(O)/2} Σ_{j=0}^∞ c_j t^{j/2} for some constants c_j.

claim: DGGW's b_0 and b_1 formulas (their equations 4.3 and 4.4) are stated as direct quotations of Donnelly [10, Thm. 5.1], not new results: b_0(γ,x)=|det(B_γ(x))| and b_1(γ,x)=|det(B_γ(x))|(⅙τ + ⅙ρ_kk + ⅓R_{iksh}B_{ki}B_{hs} + ⅓R_{ikth}B_{kt}B_{hi} - R_{kaha}B_{ks}B_{hs}).
stance_target: manuscript's normalization conventions for the b_k coefficients
scope_conditions: isometry γ of a Riemannian manifold M, fixed-point submanifold W, B_γ=(I-A_γ)^{-1}
quoted_support: Explicit formulae for b0 and b1 are given in [10, Thm. 5.1] using the following indexing conventions... (4.3) b0(γ,x)=|det(Bγ(x))| and, summing over repeated indices, (4.4) b1(γ,x)=|det(Bγ(x))|(1/6τ+1/6ρkk+1/3RikshBkiBhs+1/3RikthBktBhi−RkahaBksBhs).

claim: For a 2-orbifold cone point of order m with generator gamma, DGGW compute (Example 5.3) b_0(gamma^j) = 1/(4 sin^2(j*pi/m)) for j=1,...,m-1, matching the manuscript's claimed prefactor (1/4)csc^2(j*pi/m) exactly.
scope_conditions: cone point of order m in a 2-orbifold, N={p} single point stratum
quoted_support: b0(γj) = |det((I −Aγj)−1)| = 1/(2−2cos(2jπ/m)) = 1/(4 sin2(jπ/m)). (We are writing b0(γj) rather than using the function notation b0(γj,·) since N consists of a single point.)

claim: DGGW prove (Lemma 5.4) the trigonometric identity sum_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/sin^2(j*pi/m) = (m^2-1)/3, using the classical residue identity pi^2/sin^2(pi z) = sum_{k=-infty}^{infty} 1/(k-z)^2, citing Pennisi's 'Elements of complex variables' for the base identity.
quoted_support: A well-known formula (see, for example, [23, Example 7.9.1]), proven by the calculus of residues, states that π2/sin2(πz) = Σ_{k=−∞}^{∞} 1/(k−z)2. Thus Σ_{j=1}^{m−1} 1/sin2(jπ/m) = m2/π2 ΣΣ 1/(mk−j)2 ... the lemma follows.

claim: DGGW's Proposition 5.5 gives I_N = (m^2-1)/12 + O(t) for a single cone-point stratum N of order m, which after dividing by the isotropy order m in the master expansion (Thm 4.8) yields the degree-zero contribution (m^2-1)/(12m) -- exactly the manuscript's cone(m) formula.
scope_conditions: single cone point p of order m in a 2-orbifold
quoted_support: By 4.7(ii) and 5.3, IN = Σ_{j=1}^{m−1} 1/(4 sin2(jπ/m)) + O(t). Thus Proposition 5.5 follows from Lemma 5.4. [I_N = (m^2−1)/12 + O(t)]

claim: DGGW's full degree-zero term formula for orientable 2-orbifolds with k cone points of orders m_1,...,m_k is their equation (5.7): chi(O)/6 + sum_{i=1}^k (m_i^2-1)/(12 m_i), derived via Gauss-Bonnet a_1 = (2pi/3)chi(O).
quoted_support: By the Gauss-Bonnet Theorem (valid also for orbifolds; see [26, 30]), we have a1 = 2π/3 χ(O). Hence the degree zero term is (5.7) χ(O)/6 + Σ_{i=1}^k (m_i^2−1)/(12 m_i).

claim: DGGW give the degree-1 (order t^1) coefficient explicitly for 2-orbifolds as equation (5.10): a_2/(4pi) + sum_i R_1212*(m_i^4+10m_i^2-11)/(360 m_i) + sum_j R_1212*(n_j^4+10n_j^2-11)/(720 n_j), using the trig-sum identity sum_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/sin^4(j*pi/m) = (m^4+10m^2-11)/45 attributed to Berndt-Yeap and Chen.
stance_target: existence and exact form of the t^1 cone coefficient (b_1) in DGGW
scope_conditions: closed 2-orbifold with cone points of orders m_i and dihedral corner reflectors of orders n_j; R_1212 is the sectional curvature (=Gaussian curvature for a surface)
quoted_support: We can further simplify (5.9) by making the substitution Σ_{j=1}^{m_i-1} 1/sin4(jπ/m_i) = (m_i^4+10m_i^2−11)/45. See [3] and the references therein or [7, 16] for evaluations of this and similar finite trigonometric sums. With this substitution, (5.9) becomes (5.10) a2/4π + Σ_i R1212(m_i^4+10m_i^2−11)/360m_i + Σ_i R1212(n_i^4+10n_i^2−11)/720n_i.

claim: DGGW never present a general-l or l>=2 cone coefficient formula anywhere in the paper: the highest explicit coefficient computed is the degree-1 (t^1) term via equation (5.10), and even Table 1's worked examples (all 2-orbifolds with chi(O)>=0) truncate the expansion at O(t) or O(sqrt(t)) without numerically evaluating the t^1 term itself.
stance_target: any claim that DGGW establish b_l for l>=2 or a general-l cone coefficient
quoted_support: TABLE 1. 2-orbifold expansions with χ(O)≥0 ... O(m): V(1/t) + 1/12(2+m+1/m) + O(t) ... O(2,3,5): V(1/t) + 271/360 + O(t).

claim: DGGW record explicit spherical-2-orbifold 'near-collisions' where the degree-zero spectral invariant c=12*(degree-0 term) fails to distinguish topologically distinct orbifolds: c=4 for S^2 vs O(*3,3,3)/O(3,*3); c=5 for the good football O(2,2) vs O(*2,3,6); c=4.5 for the bad teardrop O(2) vs O(*2,4,4)/O(4,*2).
stance_target: manuscript's claim that DGGW record known spherical near-collisions
scope_conditions: closed 2-orbifolds with chi(O)>=0, spectral invariant c=2chi(O)+sum_i (m_i-1)/m_i
quoted_support: Note that for 2-orbifolds O with χ(O)=0, c is either an integer or equal to 4.5. Thus c distinguishes all but the following cases: S2 from the orbifolds O(*3,3,3) and O(3,*3) (with c=4), the good football O(2,2) from O(*2,3,6) (with c=5), and the bad teardrop O(2) from the orbifolds O(*2,4,4) and O(4,*2) (with c=4.5).

claim: DGGW's Proposition 5.22 shows that among spherical 2-orbifolds sharing a common orientable double cover (O(*m,m), O(m x), O(m*) all covering O(m,m); O(*2,2,m) and O(2,*m) covering O(2,2,m); O(*2,3,3) and O(3,*2) covering O(3,3,2)), the invariant c cannot separate members of the same nonorientable class, and separation instead requires the degree -1/2 mirror-locus term combined with a constant-curvature assumption.
stance_target: manuscript's claim about DGGW's spherical near-collision examples
quoted_support: In Table 1, c distinguishes among the remaining spherical orbifolds with the exception that c is unable to distinguish between orbifolds that are nonorientable but have the same orientable double cover: O(∗m,m), O(m×), and O(m∗), with double cover O(m,m); O(∗2,2,m) and O(2,∗m), with double cover O(2,2,m); and O(∗2,3,3) and O(3,∗2), with double cover O(3,3,2).

claim: DGGW's Proposition 5.20 proves that for closed 2-orbifolds of constant nonzero curvature, the spectrum determines the sign of the curvature, using the sign-definite t^1 coefficient formula from (5.10) when cone points or dihedral corners are present, and the degree-zero Euler characteristic term otherwise.
scope_conditions: closed 2-orbifolds of constant curvature R or -R
quoted_support: Within the class of closed 2-orbifolds of constant nonzero curvature R or −R the spectrum determines the sign of the curvature, i.e. whether the orbifold is spherical or hyperbolic. ... Notice that the summands are nonnegative, and hence we can read the sign of the curvature unless there were no cone points and no dihedral corner reflector points.

claim: DGGW's Theorem 5.1 (as originally stated in the 2008 paper, before the 2017 erratum) claims that if an orbifold's parity mismatches the parity of some singular stratum, it cannot be isospectral to a Riemannian manifold; this rests on b_0(gamma,x) being strictly positive on the stratum for gamma in Isomax(N).
scope_conditions: even/odd dimensional orbifold with an odd/even dimensional stratum
quoted_support: 5.1. THEOREM. Let O be a Riemannian orbifold with singularities. If O is even dimensional (respectively, odd dimensional) and some O-stratum of the singular set is odd dimensional (respectively, even dimensional), then O cannot be isospectral to a Riemannian manifold. Proof. It is clear from (4.3) that if N is any O-stratum of the singular set, then the function b0(γ,·) is strictly positive on N for each γ∈Isomax(N).

claim: DGGW's References list cites Donnelly's 1976 paper exactly as: 'H. Donnelly, Spectrum and the fixed point sets of isometries I, Math. Ann. 224 (1976), 161-170,' matching the manuscript's citation.
quoted_support: [10] H. Donnelly, Spectrum and the fixed point sets of isometries I, Math. Ann. 224 (1976), 161–170.

claim: DGGW's degree -1/2 term (from the one-dimensional mirror locus) is given as equation (5.11): coefficient = length(MirrorLocus(O))/(8*sqrt(pi)), derived from b_0(gamma,x)=1/2 for a reflection isometry.
stance_target: completeness of DGGW's low-order coefficient list
quoted_support: We sum over all O-strata of the mirror locus to obtain the coefficient of the 1/sqrt(t) term in Theorem 4.8: (5.11) Σ_N I_N/|Iso(N)| = Σ_N (1/2)(length(N)/4√π) = length(MirrorLocus(O))/8√π.
